title: Chess, But I Can Use Portals
summary: Original Portal chess vs Stockfish: the player can use Portal 2-style portals - a blue and an orange portal placed on empty squares; a piece moving into one instantly exits from the other, so e.g. 1.e4 can effectively be 1.d4 and a rook on b1 can instantly be on h1. Portals may not be placed on occupied squares (otherwise you could capture the king turn one). Stockfish does not know about the portals. Narrator teleports pawns and pieces next to the castled black king (h6, queen to h6, knight drop to e8) and wins his one game.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only the player has portals.
Two linked portals: blue and orange. Each can be placed on an EMPTY square only.
A piece whose move ends on a portal square is instantly transported to the other portal's square (must be able to legally reach the entry square with its normal move).

Portal placement is done as part of the player's turn - placing both then moving through them in the same turn appears allowed ('make a portal on D2 and then drop the knight on E8, gives check') [inferred: no move cost].
The engine is unaware of portals.

current_impl_issues: Legacy 'portals' uses fixed linked portals that teleport any piece (both sides) stopping on one. Real: player-placed portals on empty squares, used only by the player, repositionable each turn.
